title: Wicflow hero explainer: the work, in blocks (storyboard v2)
logline: A company’s real work (quotes going quiet, enquiries piling up, hours typed in twice) becomes its own shape in Wicflow’s block world, where off-the-shelf software won’t sit. The AI mapping lays the processes out, watches the time drain from each, and finds the highest return. The costed plan ranks it first, lies down as the ground, and its top row rises as the periwinkle first block, guaranteed. Inside that block the quote follow-up runs on its own. Block by block the system builds, each block with its automation running, until all of it is connected. Then it shrinks above the wicflow lockup and unbuilds back into the work, so the film loops.

changes_v2.feedback: Karl on v1: “I like it, but it’s too much text. I want it more SaaS-like: text here and there, but the majority visualising what the voice-over says, or what the platform literally is. Also, give me 1 image with the whole storyboard.”
changes: Text budget: three text moments outside the product UI for the whole film (limit five): ‘First block · guaranteed’ (B5), ‘All of it connected’ (B8) and the end lockup (B9). v1 had a headline or kinetic line in nine of ten beats.
The left headline column is gone from every beat. The voice-over carries the words, and the subject is centred and fills at least half the frame.
B1 now shows the company’s real work literally: a quote going quiet, enquiries piling up, hours re-typed into an invoice, a report built by hand (abstract content, no names or figures).
B2 shows ‘off the shelf’ as a generic app slab that cannot sit on the company’s shape. ‘Built around how you work’ is a measuring scan, not a headline.
B3 is now the AI mapping as an interface: the processes as a flow, time draining from each, the highest return found. The kinetic-type headline and the chip row are gone.
B4 is the costed plan as a clean UI card, with glyph column heads; the ‘A costed plan’ / ‘Highest return first.’ headlines are gone.
B6 shows the automation running end to end: an open quote → a drafted follow-up → ready for the salesperson, paying off B1’s quiet quote.
B7 shows each block priced in writing (a signed price document) and its automation running (hours to invoices, the weekly report building itself), replacing the headline and the list.
B9 is a centred lockup under the shrunken system; ‘300+ projects built’ is off the screen.

Dropped from the screen: ‘Software made to work for every company / never quite fits yours’, ‘Built around how you work’, ‘Custom automation and AI…’, ‘AI MAPPING · FIXED PRICE · 1–2 WEEKS’, ‘First we map where the time goes’, ‘No open quote goes quiet’, ‘Drafts ready for the salesperson’, ‘Every block priced in writing…’, ‘One system’, ‘In your name and colours’, ‘Hosted in Finland’, ‘One contact at Wicflow’, ‘300+ projects built’. ‘Hosted in Finland’ also left the VO, because it has no literal picture in the film.
New: one overview image of the whole storyboard (site/storyboard-overview.png). v1 is kept as storyboard_v1.json; its frames are in git history.

textBudget.uiTextRule: Product-UI text is small (Fragment Mono 20–26 for chips and tags, Inter 34–36 for a panel title or row label) and appears only where a real interface would show it: Open, AI mapping, Week 1 · Week 2, Costed plan, the five row labels, First block, Quote follow-ups, Running, Draft ready, and the block numbers.

beats.name: The real work
beats.vo: Quotes go quiet. Enquiries pile up. Hours get typed in twice.
uiText: Open (status chip on the quote card)
beats.onScreen: No text outside the product UI. UI only: the status chip ‘Open’ on the quote card.
beats.visual: The company’s real work, big and centred: four opaque glass cards (520×320) fill x 430–1510, y 160–930. A quote, an enquiry inbox, hours beside an invoice, and the owner’s report, all drawn from placeholder bars and icons (no names, no figures). Each card acts out its VO line literally. The quote’s reply bubble empties and its activity trace decays to a flat line: it goes quiet. New enquiries drop onto the inbox and pile up, each with an orange unread dot. A cursor re-types a highlighted row of hours into the invoice. A cursor drags a report bar up by hand.
beats.motion: 0.00: the cards are already drifting (6 px and ±1.5° on a 3.76 s period, phase-offset), so frame 0 moves. 0.40–1.60: the quote card comes forward (×1 → ×1.18, B4 spring, damping 200) while the others dim to 28%; its timer ring drains to 10% and turns peach, the bubble’s three dots fade out one by one (0.12 s stagger) and the activity trace decays left to right. 1.70–2.20: the quote steps back to 55%; seven enquiries drop onto the inbox, one every 0.07 s, each settling 3 px with no bounce. 2.20–2.90: a row of hours outlines, a dashed arrow draws to the invoice, and the cursor types the line with a caret. 2.60–3.20: on the report, the cursor drags the last bar up in two moves. A new event lands every 0.5–0.6 s.
beats.transitionOut: 3.30–3.90: the four cards flatten into the top faces of four wireframe blocks (QUOTE → 01, ENQUIRY → 02, HOURS → 04, REPORT → 05) while the wire world draws itself around them.

beats.name: Off the shelf never fits
beats.vo: Off-the-shelf software never quite fits. We build around how you work.
beats.visual: The work becomes the company’s own shape: the reference’s 14 wireframe blocks, now centred (x 600–1320, y 170–971). A generic, one-size-fits-all app, a grey slab whose top face is a standard app window (title-bar dots, a sidebar, a uniform tile grid), lowers onto the stepped shape and cannot sit: it strikes the tallest block (orange outline) and leaves orange gaps above the lower blocks. It slides away. A periwinkle scan band then passes over the wire blocks; the edges it touches are measured (small dimension ticks) and settle crisp. That is ‘built around how you work’, shown rather than written.
beats.motion: 3.60–4.40: the wire world draws on back to front (0.06 s stagger, dashes marching at 12 px/s) as the cards land on their top faces and fade into them. 4.60–5.20: the slab lowers from above (ease-out, 0.5 s). 5.20: contact, a 3 px settle, block 06 flashes orange and the gap lines draw down (0.2 s). 5.40–5.90: hold, with a soft ‘wrong’ tick. 5.90–6.30: the slab lifts and slides out to the right (ease-in). 6.30–7.40: the scan band sweeps front-left to back-right; the edges under it brighten and two dimension ticks pop (0.15 s each).
beats.transitionOut: 7.40–7.80: the top faces of the five named blocks lift and flatten into the AI mapping’s process tiles.

frames.caption: The work lands on the company’s own shape.
frames.draw: The wire world centred on the lattice (960 + 120(i−j), 554 + 69.5(i+j) − 128h), some blocks still drawing (progress 0.35–1). The four cards are 74% of the way onto the top faces of blocks 01, 02, 04 and 05, opaque navy, contents at 18%, edges periwinkle.

frames.caption: Off-the-shelf software never quite fits.
frames.draw: A 3×3 grey slab (side faces rgba(140–160,148–168,166–186,.42–.48)) at h 2.7–3. Its top face carries a generic app window mapped onto the rhombus: three title-bar dots, a sidebar and a 3×3 grid of identical tiles. Block 06 shows through in orange #FF5A1F; four orange dashed gap lines drop from the slab’s underside to the lower blocks, each ending in a dot.

beats.name: The AI mapping
beats.vo: First, we map where the time goes.
beats.onScreen: No text outside the product UI. UI only, small: the window title ‘AI mapping’ and ‘Week 1’ · ‘Week 2’ on its progress track.
beats.visual: The AI mapping as an interface, big (window x 220–1700, y 140–940). The company’s five processes are laid out as a flow of icon tiles (new customers → enquiries → quotes → hours → report), linked by curves with data dots running. Time drains out of every process: peach drops (the site’s accent colour, used here for time) fall from each tile into its own column on a time axis. A scan line moves with the Week 1 → Week 2 track. When the track ends, the quotes column is the tallest: corner brackets lock onto the quotes tile, it turns periwinkle, its column turns periwinkle and glows, and the rest dim. There are no figures anywhere.
beats.motion: 7.60–8.20: the five top faces fly up and flatten into tiles (0.06 s stagger, soft settle) while the window draws its outline. 8.20–8.60: the connectors draw and the data dots start. 8.60–10.20: drops fall (gravity ease-in, two or three per tile per second) and the columns rise; the scan line and the week track move together. 10.30: the brackets snap onto quotes (0.2 s, 2 px settle); the tile and its column cross-fade to periwinkle and the others dim to 36% (0.3 s). 10.50–11.10: a pulse ring breathes around the quotes tile.
beats.transitionOut: 11.10–11.40: the window resizes into the costed plan card; the five tiles drop into the rows’ icon slots in the same left-to-right order.

Five glass tiles with line icons (person-plus, chat, document, clock, chart) linked by S-curves with white data dots. Below each tile, peach drops fall into a peach column on the baseline y 872 (a small clock glyph marks the axis); the columns stand at 28–66% of their final heights. A scan line at x 1100 with a soft periwinkle band behind it.

beats.name: The costed plan
beats.vo: A costed plan. Highest return first.
uiText: Quote follow-ups · Enquiries answered · New customers · Hours to invoices · Owner’s weekly report (row labels)
beats.onScreen: No text outside the product UI. UI only: the card title ‘Costed plan’, the five row labels (the site’s Kallio Lämpö blocks) and the tag ‘First block’. The column heads are glyphs: a trend arrow over the returns, ‘€’ over the costs.
beats.visual: A clean plan card (x 380–1540, y 140–940). Five rows, each an icon tile, a label, a periwinkle return bar and a grey cost bar. The bars are schematic, with no figures. The rows arrive in the mapping’s order, with quotes already lit. Then the re-rank: the quote row lifts on a plate and glides to the top while new customers slides down. The ranked list ends with Quote follow-ups highlighted and tagged ‘First block’, and a sheen runs along its bar.
beats.motion: 11.20–11.90: the rows slide in from the right (0.06 s stagger), their bars growing (B11 fill, 0.5 s). 12.40–13.40: the re-rank. The quote row lifts 12 px on a plate with a deeper shadow and scales to 1.025, glides up two slots (B4 spring, 0.6 s), and new customers slides down behind it at 60%. 13.50: the plate settles into a periwinkle highlight and the tag ‘First block’ pops in (0.2 s). 13.90–14.60: a sheen runs along the top bar; the other rows ease to 62%.
beats.transitionOut: 14.90–15.40: the card tilts back on its bottom edge and lies down as the iso ground (the signature move); its top row stays lifted.

frames.caption: The plan forms in the mapping’s order.
frames.draw: Card: glass rgba(255,255,255,.05), radius 32. Title ‘Costed plan’ (Stack Sans Headline 44). Rows at y 350/470/590/710/830 in map order (new customers, enquiries, quotes, hours, report); the quotes tile is lit periwinkle; the bars stand at 30–75% of their length; the last two rows are still sliding in (30 and 70 px right, 75% and 45%).

frames.caption: Highest return first: the re-rank.
frames.draw: The quote row rides a lifted plate (#1A2246, deep shadow, ×1.025) at y 398, on its way to the top. New customers slides down behind it at 60% (y 548); enquiries stays at 85%; hours and report sit in their slots.

beats.name: First block, guaranteed
beats.vo: First block, guaranteed. Not as agreed? You don’t pay.
uiText: Quote follow-ups (row label at 50%, on the tilting plan only)
beats.onScreen: TEXT MOMENT 1: the leader label ‘First block · guaranteed’ (Fragment Mono 32), exactly as in the reference.
beats.visual: The signature move. The plan card tilts back and lies down as the iso ground; its top row lifts off the plane, and from where its icon was, the first block rises: periwinkle, studded, the only coloured block in the film. The rest of the company stands around it as wireframe. A glint crosses its stud, and a thin leader line drops to the label, as in the reference.
beats.motion: 15.20–15.80: the card tilts onto the floor plane (whipOut, 0.6 s) while the top row lifts 64 px with a soft shadow. 15.80–16.20: the row folds into the footprint of cell (0,2) and the floor grid dashes in. 16.20–16.90: the first block extrudes upward (B4 spring, damping 200, no overshoot) with a plastic ‘thock’, its stud rising last. 16.90–17.60: the other 13 blocks draw in as dashed wire, back to front. 17.70: a glint arcs across the stud. 17.90: the leader line draws down (0.25 s) and the label types on (0.3 s). It holds, alive, until 19.30 (dashes marching, glow breathing).
beats.transitionOut: 19.30–19.50: zoom through block 01’s top face (B16, 16 frames, cut on the fastest frame); the face becomes the automation panel.

frames.caption: The plan lies down as the ground.
frames.draw: The card mid-tilt: its corners 55% of the way to the floor rhombus (left (600,762.5), top (960,554), right (1320,762.5), bottom (960,971)), dashed 3×3 grid, faint row traces. The top row is lifted 64 px off the plane: periwinkle glass with a #B9C1FF border, its content (icon tile, ‘Quote follow-ups’, bar) at 50%, a soft periwinkle glow at its left end.

frames.caption: The first block rises.
frames.draw: The floor grid only (dashed). Block 01 at cell (0,2,0) in PERI (top #CDD3FF, left #B9C1FF, right #98A2F5), its stud still rising (14 of 20 px), glow at 60%. Two neighbouring wire blocks are just beginning to draw (10–25%).

frames.caption: First block · guaranteed.
frames.draw: All 14 blocks: 13 dashed wire, block 01 PERI with a 60 px glow and a white glint on its stud. Leader: 1.2 px rgba(223,230,243,.5) from the block’s left-front corner (600,764) down to a periwinkle dot at (600,932); label ‘First block · guaranteed’ in Fragment Mono 32 at x 620.

beats.name: Inside the block, it runs
beats.vo: Then it runs. No open quote goes quiet.
beats.onScreen: No text outside the product UI. UI only: the panel title ‘Quote follow-ups’, the status chip ‘Running’, the chip ‘Open’ on the quote and the tag ‘Draft ready’.
beats.visual: Through the first block into the automation, big (panel x 240–1680, y 160–920, periwinkle-tinted glass, a small periwinkle block glyph by its title). It reads left to right: an open quote, at the front of a queue of quotes → the follow-up drafts itself (sparkle tile, lines typing) → it lands in the salesperson’s queue, tagged ‘Draft ready’ with a send button. The quote’s timer ring refills in periwinkle and gets a check: the payoff of B1’s quiet quote.
beats.motion: 19.40–19.67: the panel grows from 62% to 100% (whipOut, 16 frames) with radial streaks in the first 6. 19.80: the Running dot starts pulsing (1.2 s). 19.90–20.40: data dots run from the quote to the draft card. 20.30–21.60: the draft types itself, line by line, with a caret. 21.60–21.90: its send button fills periwinkle, and dots run on to the salesperson. 21.90–22.20: the queue card slides in (B3, 0.3 s) with ‘Draft ready’; the quote’s ring refills and a check pops. 22.30–22.90: a sheen crosses ‘Draft ready’; the next quote slides forward in the queue, so it keeps running.
beats.transitionOut: 22.93–23.20: the panel shrinks back into block 01’s top face (reverse zoom-through, 16 frames); the world returns with 01 glowing.

frames.caption: Through the block, into the automation.
frames.draw: The giant PERI top face leaves through the four frame corners (#CDD3FF at 35%). The automation panel at 62% scale, centred, its contents blurred (3 px), with 32 radial streaks around it.

frames.caption: An open quote → a drafted follow-up.
frames.draw: Panel header: periwinkle block glyph, ‘Quote follow-ups’ (Inter 500 34), and ‘Running’ (green #16B857 dot with a pulse ring, Fragment Mono 24). Stage 1: a quote card (300×400, #151D3D) in front of two queued cards, with a peach timer ring at 40% and the chip ‘Open’. Stage 2: the draft card with a glowing sparkle tile, its five lines 55% typed and a periwinkle caret. Stage 3: the salesperson avatar at 55% above a dashed, empty queue slot.

frames.caption: Ready for the salesperson.
frames.draw: Draft fully typed, its send button #6172F3. Stage 3 lit: the avatar ring periwinkle, and a queue card with a mini draft, the tag ‘Draft ready’ (#6172F3, Fragment Mono 22) under a sheen, and a send button. The quote card’s border is periwinkle, its ring refilled at 100% and a check badge on its corner. Both connectors are lit with data dots.

beats.name: Block by block
beats.vo: Block by block, each priced in writing before we start.
uiText: Block numbers 01–05 printed on the faces
beats.onScreen: No text outside the product UI. Only the block numbers 01–05 printed on the faces, and ‘04’ on the hours card.
beats.visual: Back out in the world. Before a block builds, a document with a price line is signed beside it (the signature draws itself), and only then does the block fill from the top down: priced in writing before we start. Each finished block shows its automation running. Hours from the timesheet fly straight into invoice lines, with no cursor (block 04, its card beside the world). The owner’s weekly report draws its own bars (block 05, its card unfolding above it). Block 06 stays dashed wire until everything connects.
beats.motion: 23.20–23.47: the world settles from ×4 to ×1 with 01 glowing. 23.50–24.10: the price document slides in to the right of block 02 (B3) and its signature draws (0.5 s); a dashed tether points at 02, which brightens from the top down (wipe, 0.4 s). 24.30–24.70: block 03 does the same, faster. 24.70–25.60: the world eases left to ×0.9 as 04 lands; a light line climbs from its stud and folds into the hours card; cells fly into the invoice one after another (0.12 s apart) and its lines fill. 25.70–26.10: the world returns to centre; 05 lands. 26.10–26.90: a light line draws from 05 to the report card, whose bars rise by themselves, with a sparkle tile and no cursor (the B1 contrast). Rising clicks, one per block.
beats.transitionOut: 26.80–27.10: the cards fold back into their blocks; their light lines stay and become the system’s connections.

A dashed periwinkle tether runs to block 02’s right face.

A 5×6 timesheet; three periwinkle cells mid-flight along a dotted arc into the invoice, whose first three lines are filled and whose fourth is filling.

frames.caption: The weekly report builds itself.

beats.name: All of it connected
beats.vo: One system. All of it connected.
beats.onScreen: TEXT MOMENT 2: the leader label ‘All of it connected’ at the top block (Fragment Mono 32), as in reference 4.
beats.visual: The blocks connect: periwinkle light lines climb between them, block to block, and the top block 06 becomes solid when the last line reaches it. One pulse travels through the system and lights every stud. The leader line rises from 06 to its label, as in the reference. The system holds, glowing, with pulses circulating.
beats.motion: 27.00–28.10: light lines draw 01→02→03→05 and 01→04→06 (0.25 s each, sparks at their heads), each landing with a tone. 28.10–28.40: 06 fills from glass to SOLID. 28.40–28.90: one wave ring spreads from 06 and every stud lights in turn (an arpeggio). 28.60: the top leader draws up (0.25 s) and the label types on. 29.00–30.70: the stack grows to ×1.04 (slow ease) while pulses circulate the lines.
beats.transitionOut: 30.70–31.30: the system breathes out and rises, shrinking toward the top of the frame to make room for the lockup.

frames.caption: The blocks connect.
frames.draw: Blocks 01–05 as in 26.40, 06 glass. Light lines (#B9C1FF over a 10 px blurred periwinkle) are complete for 01–02 and 02–03, and 78%, 50% and 20% along 01–04, 03–05 and 04–06, each with a white spark at its head. Solid studs sit on top of the lines.

frames.caption: All of it connected.
frames.draw: Every line complete. 06 SOLID with a stronger glow; a soft wave ring around its top; studs 01–04 lit white; two sparks travelling. Leader: from 06’s stud up to a dot at (960,112); the label ‘All of it connected’ ends at x 940 (Fragment Mono 32).

frames.caption: One system, alive.
frames.draw: The lit system at ×1.04: every block lit, a halo behind 06, three pulses on the lines. The label holds (8 px higher, following the scale).

beats.name: Let’s find the first thing to build
beats.vo: Let’s find the first thing to build. Book an AI mapping.
textOutsideUI: Let’s find the first thing to build.
beats.onScreen: TEXT MOMENT 3, the end lockup, centred: the wicflow mark and wordmark, one line ‘Let’s find the first thing to build.’ and the button ‘Book an AI mapping →’.
beats.visual: The lit system shrinks and rises to sit above the lockup, like a product above its name. Then the wicflow mark and wordmark, the one line and the white button arrive, centred. Pulses keep running through the small system, so the end card is never still; a sheen crosses the button.
beats.motion: 30.80–31.80: the system scales ×1.04 → ×0.5 and rises 238 px (smooth ease-in-out, 1 s). 31.90–32.40: the mark reveals (a soft radial wipe) and the wordmark fades up 12 px (A5). 32.70: the line rises in (0.4 s). 33.20: the button scales from 96% to 100% (B4) with a resolving chord. 34.00–34.60: a sheen crosses the button and its arrow nudges 3 px. It holds, alive, to 35.60.
beats.transitionOut: 35.60–35.90: the lockup fades out (ease-in, 0.3 s) and the small system starts to unbuild.

beats.name: Back to the work (loop)
beats.vo: (none: the tail of the music bed carries the loop)
beats.visual: The system unbuilds back into the work. The small world fades through glass to wire while the top faces of blocks 01, 02, 04 and 05 lift off and grow back into the four work cards: the exact layout of frame 0, so the film loops.
beats.motion: 35.80–36.20: the blocks drain from solid to glass to wire, in reverse build order. 36.00–37.40: the four faces lift and unfold into the cards along the B1→B2 path in reverse (B3 settle; their drift phase matches frame 0). 37.40–37.60: the last of the wire fades. 37.60 ≡ 0.00 (frame 2256 = frame 0); the 3.76 s card drift runs ten periods per loop, so pose and velocity match.

notes: What changed in v2. v2 keeps v1’s story, timing (37.6 s, ten beats) and block-world thread. It answers Karl’s note “too much text” by moving every word into the voice-over except three text moments, and by making each beat show its VO line literally, or show the platform itself, big and centred. The 3D block beats (B2, B5, B7, B8) alternate with large flat UI beats (B1, B3, B4, B6), and one element still becomes the next: cards → block faces → mapping tiles → plan rows → the ground → the first block → its automation → the world → the lockup → the cards.

Look, from wicflow.com’s CSS and references 1–4. One still radial background, centred (960,540), #131C3A → #0E1630 (45%) → #0B1220, with 2% static dither; it never moves. Text #F3F5FA; muted text rgba(223,230,243,.72); lines rgba(255,255,255,.10). The work cards are opaque navy glass (#161F3F, 1 px rgba(255,255,255,.14), radius 26); the UI windows are glass (rgba(255,255,255,.045–.05), radius 32, even shadow). Periwinkle #6172F3 → #B9C1FF is Wicflow’s colour: return bars, highlights and the first block. Peach (#ffd9c8 → #f3a585, the site’s accent-word gradient) is time: the mapping’s drains and the quiet quote’s ring. Orange #FF5A1F appears only for problems: unread enquiries and the misfit slab. Green #16B857 appears only on ‘Running’. Icons are 2.5 px round-cap line icons in a 48-unit box.

Block rules. Orthographic 2:1 isometric, now centred: a lattice point (i,j,h) sits at (960 + 120(i−j), 554 + 69.5(i+j) − 128h); the silhouette spans x 600–1320, y 170–971 (74% of the frame height). Fourteen blocks as in the reference: 01 Quote follow-ups (0,2,0), the first block; 02 Enquiries answered (2,2,0); 03 New customers (2,0,1); 04 Hours to invoices (0,1,1); 05 Owner’s weekly report (1,0,1); 06 One system (0,0,2). States: WIRE (dashed 6/6, marching 12 px/s), GLASS, SOLID (#F2F3FC/#DCDFF5/#C2C7EC with its number), GLASS-PERI and PERI (#CDD3FF/#B9C1FF/#98A2F5), only ever for 01. Card ↔ block: QUOTE → 01, ENQUIRY → 02, HOURS → 04, REPORT → 05. The mapping’s tiles come from the five named blocks’ top faces.

Type and layout. Outside the UI only three text moments: the two leader labels (Fragment Mono 32, sentence case, a 1.2 px rgba(223,230,243,.5) line and a 9 px dot, as in the references) and the end lockup (the mark, ‘wicflow’ in Manrope 800 92 px as the site’s nav sets it, the line in Stack Sans Headline 500 60 px, the button in Inter 600 38 px). UI text: Inter 500 34–36 for a panel title or row label, Fragment Mono 20–26 for chips, tags and the week track. Everything essential sits inside x 96–1824, y 54–1026, and the subject is at least half the frame. For Finnish, the UI labels run 25–35% longer: the plan rows have room to 560 px, and the lockup line reflows to two lines at 60 px.

Motion identity: calm, clean, Apple. Arrivals decelerate (ARRIVE cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)); exits accelerate (ease-in, 0.2–0.3 s); landings end in a 2–4 px drift with no overshoot (B4 spring, damping 200). No bounce, elastic, anticipation or camera pans. The scale moves are the B1 focus pull, the two zoom-throughs of block 01 (16 frames each way) and the B7 and B9 eases. A new visual lands every 0.5–0.8 s; holds stay alive (drift, marching dashes, data dots, pulses). Motion norm: the house 7% median (motion_check.py at 60 fps); test B2 and B5, the thinnest wire beats, first at the animatic. Sound: effects lead over a quiet music bed (louder with no VO), from films/alumni/sound/lib: soft ticks as the enquiries pile up, keyboard taps for the re-typing, a dull thud and a ‘wrong’ tick on the slab, droplet ticks for the time drains, a lock-on click on the found tile, a card-shuffle swish on the re-rank, a deep whoosh and a plastic ‘thock’ on the tilt, typing ticks and a soft ding on ‘Draft ready’, a pen scratch on each signature, rising clicks block by block, an arpeggio as the studs light, a resolving chord under the lockup, and a reverse shimmer into the loop.

Truth, exclusions and loop. Every on-screen phrase comes from wicflow.com: ‘First block · guaranteed’, ‘All of it connected’, ‘Let’s find the first thing to build’, ‘Book an AI mapping’, ‘AI mapping’, ‘Week 1’ / ‘Week 2’, ‘costed plan’, the five Kallio Lämpö block names, ‘First block’, ‘Quote follow-ups’ and ‘Drafts ready for the salesperson’ (as the tag ‘Draft ready’). There are no figures on screen: the bars and columns are schematic, and every card is placeholder bars and icons. Kallio Lämpö is the site’s made-up heating company; the plan shows its blocks. The VO uses the site’s facts (‘first block, guaranteed’, ‘if it doesn’t do what we agreed, you don’t pay’, ‘no open quote goes quiet’, ‘every block priced in writing before we start’, ‘all of it connected’); B1’s problem lines are the site’s block promises turned around (see the open questions). EXCLUDED, from Wicflow’s current hero: stock footage of real work (a forklift, a tractor), a headline over full-bleed video, a linear drift over stock, and the cycling word. Also out: generic AI imagery, cartoon icons, bounce, invented names or figures, and the site’s other example companies. Loop: 37.60 ≡ 0.00 (frame 2256 = frame 0).
questions: B1’s VO, ‘Quotes go quiet. Enquiries pile up. Hours get typed in twice.’, turns the site’s block promises around (‘No open quote goes quiet’, ‘Every enquiry answered the same day by the right person’, ‘Hours from the sites go straight into invoices’). Is Wicflow happy to say the problems this plainly, or should B1’s VO be the softer ‘Every company loses time somewhere.’ (the pictures stay the same)?

Hero videos usually autoplay muted. v2 tells the story in pictures, and the VO carries the words, so a muted visitor gets the pictures and the three text moments. Should the hero carry optional subtitles (a captions track, or small burned-in lines) for muted autoplay, or is the picture story enough?

With the text column gone, the film can play full-bleed behind the hero headline ‘Built for the work that keeps your company on schedule.’ in place of the stock video, or as its own player beside it. Which? Full-bleed would need the subject kept clear of the headline’s side.
Should the end button be ‘Book an AI mapping’ (as boarded: the story’s next step and the site’s main button) or the hero’s own ‘Get your free AI roadmap’?
‘Hosted in Finland’ and ‘One contact at Wicflow’ have left the film, because they have no literal picture. Keep them out, or add ‘…hosted in Finland’ back to B8’s VO without a visual?

The return bars and time columns are schematic (no figures) and follow the site’s 01–05 order, so they imply that this is Kallio Lämpö’s payback order. Acceptable, or should every bar except the first be the same length?

styleframes.source: frames-src/ (frame.html?f=<id> draws each key frame as a 1920×1080 SVG with Wicflow’s fonts and mark; lib.js is the isometric block engine, now centred; frames.js has one function per v2 frame; render.js renders them with Playwright to site/frames/*.jpg at 1600 px). make_overview.py builds the one-image overview.
styleframes.fonts: Stack Sans Headline, Inter, Fragment Mono and Manrope 800 (the nav wordmark), all from wicflow.com, in films/wicflow/harvest/
deviations: B1 1.20: the quiet quote’s activity trace hangs just below the card, so it reads at hero size; in the film it can sit inside the card’s footer.
B7 25.00: the world eases left to ×0.9 to make room for the hours card. It is the only beat where the world leaves the centre, and it returns by 25.70.
B10 36.40: the cards are drawn opaque during the morph so the world behind does not show through them.
